idee_recherchee.texte: The Big Bang was not an explosion in space but the rapid expansion of space itself from an extremely hot and dense state about 13.8 billion years ago, and the question of what came before it remains unanswered.

titre_video: Scientists Are Freaking Out Over Space Time (It's Not Real)
titre: Une hypothèse : l'évaporation des trous noirs
resume: Primordial black holes are only hypothetical, since the universe is about 13.7 or 13.8 billion years old and nobody can know what happened moments after the Big Bang. Some cosmologists propose that black holes have a lifespan and may evaporate through quantum mechanical processes, smaller ones faster, so many primordial ones may have vanished long ago.
texte: To be fair, primordial black holes are only hypothetical as scientists believe that our universe is around 13.7 or 13.8 billion years old and there is currently no way to know what happened moments after the Big Bang. Some cosmologists have proposed the idea that primordial black holes and all black holes for that matter might have a lifespan and due to quantum mechanical processes may eventually evaporate out of existence if there isn't enough matter around them to consume. Smaller black holes are predicted to evaporate more quickly than larger ones, but either way, the remnants of many primordial black holes may have disappeared from existence long ago.
